summary.name: Docker
summary.one_liner: Docker is a container platform for building, sharing, and running applications, now also offering MicroVM-isolated sandboxes, governance, and hardened images for AI agents.
use_cases: Running isolated AI agent sessions locally or in the cloud
Governing sandbox and MCP server policies across a team
Using signed, minimal container base images
Moving agent workloads from laptop to cloud sandboxes
Auditing agent actions with identity-bound logs
summary.what_it_does: The page describes Docker as a platform for building, sharing, and running container applications, with the goal of handling setup so developers can focus on code. It promotes Docker Sandboxes, which provide MicroVM isolation for each agent session with network and filesystem restrictions enforced at runtime. Docker AI Governance offers one console for sandbox and MCP policy with identity-bound audit logs. Docker Hardened Images are described as minimal, signed, continuously patched images and MCP servers meeting SLSA Level 3. The page states the platform is OCI-compliant and platform-independent.
notable: MicroVM isolation for AI agent sessions, local or cloud
Docker Hardened Images: signed, minimal, SLSA Level 3
Centralized console for sandbox and MCP policy with audit logs
caveats: Pricing is not stated on the page
Much of the page is marketing claims without technical detail on how features are implemented
Listing in awesome-mac describes it as Freeware and open source, which the page itself does not confirm
